### application-core values V1 step 1: the interpreter's Strings are UTF-16 code units, as the JVM's

change `lkvnqurnqwwt` · [log `e7462bae943c`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/e7462bae943c2fc14612b7931c07fe16b8926837fa9ce28eafa038792bc45888.jsonl.gz)

The interpreter, which replays every witness, held a String as Rust UTF-8 text, so every isolated surrogate became U+FFFD: "\uD800".equals("\uFFFD") and "\uD800".equals("\uDC00") were true, charAt gave 65533, and a surrogate pair split by substring became two U+FFFD. Now interp::JStr holds a String's and a StringBuilder's code units, and every modelled operation works on them as the JDK's do: StringBuilder.reverse keeps a pair together, indexOf(int) takes a supplementary code point, strip and isBlank use Character.isWhitespace's set, new String(char[]) and its siblings are modelled, append(CharSequence, int, int) is refused instead of appending the whole sequence, and setLength(-1) throws. An operation that needs Unicode's tables (case conversion, equalsIgnoreCase, number syntax) is refused on a String with an isolated surrogate, and Integer.parseInt on any non-ASCII code unit (Character.digit takes every Unicode digit), rather than answered for other text. Messages that quote a String keep its units, and Objects.requireNonNull's message is the very String given. Machine::str_of keeps its signature, now for readers; Machine::units_of is what a String is.

Reproducer first: lib/tests/values.rs, the values stream's model conformance test, runs 67 small String methods (lib/tests/fixtures/values/) on a real JVM and in the interpreter and requires the same code units, or a refusal where one is listed. Before the fix, 28 cases differed and one was refused; now all agree. The full lib suite passes (cargo test: 476 tests, the integration contract application_core.rs included). The audit of what native runs faithfully, two wrong answers found outside V1's core (Character's classification uses Rust's Unicode tables, and a surrogate char renders as U+FFFD in a contract), and an interface request for the merge (the class reader decodes a string literal lossily) are in the brief's Progress. Next: the own checker's bounded Strings.

### application-core values V1 step 2: the own checker's Strings are bounded code units with content, and a String parameter has every content up to its bound

change `ltwqxnvqzzno` · [log `b4891f44f078`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/b4891f44f07816f6eb12d1e8f801be6cae6c4e790986af5778936ff4ff956dae.jsonl.gz)

In the native engine (lib/src/bmc/), a String is now an object whose content is UTF-16 code units of a symbolic length, a char cell per unit it may have, any of the 65,536 values. The content reuses the arrays' machinery for merging, aliasing and witnesses, and Obj::content/as_array keep a String apart from an array. A literal has its units. length, isEmpty, charAt (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException), equals (identity, null, another class, then the lengths and every unit) and startsWith (NullPointerException on null) are modelled on content, through bmc::models_string_method, which the gap scan shares. A compiler-generated concatenation of Strings, null, chars and constants has its parts' content. A number concatenated gives a String with no content, whose methods stay the jdk-primitive-method gap. One that could pass bmc::MAX_STRING_CONTENT (64) units ends with a named limit wherever its content is asked for, never a truncated String. A harness String parameter is taken only under an explicit bound, the new bmc::Parameters::max_string_length; None refuses it by name. It has every content up to the bound, the same nullable and may-alias options as an array, and its witness is its code units in raw_arrays.

Reproducer: before, every String parameter was outside the fragment (bmc::unsupported_parameter), and String.length/charAt/equals were gaps. The new tests in lib/tests/values.rs run the checker on harness-shaped methods (lib/tests/fixtures/values/values/Checks.java), merging paths from the start and never. Every violation's witness is replayed on the JVM (ValuesRunner now takes String, null and same-object arguments) and in the interpreter, and must throw the check's AssertionError. The quote fixture's Codes.vip rewrite is proved up to 5 units, and its dropped-prefix defect refuted with 'VI' plus a unit that isn't 'P'. An isolated surrogate and 'A\\0' are found as inputs. A defect that takes a surrogate pair for one unit is refuted with the pair. Equal content behind distinct references refutes an identity claim. Further cases cover charAt's bounds, startsWith(null), null Strings, the bound (proved under 4, refuted with 5 units under 5), and concatenation up to the cap and past it. The gap scan counts the modelled methods as no gap. Evidence level: tested. The whole lib suite passes (lib unit 226, alignment 34, application_core 14, compare 1, conformance 10, effects 18, foundations 5, heap 49, integration 65, observations 12, skill 1, summaries 40, values 8).

### application-core values V1 step 3: the String value adapter, its domain, evidence, witness reader, encoding and rebuilding

change `nlkuyptrtrmy` · [log `e0c1ceae0ea7`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/e0c1ceae0ea7ef5b6d37ad79027360d66a828f00ee9bc0703afbd076e59f5972.jsonl.gz)

values::StringAdapter (lib/src/values.rs) is the String's value adapter: a spec::plans::ValueDomain of kind string with its bound, nullability and the model's evidence (values::string_model: the model identity STRING_MODEL, JDK 25.0.5 sampled, level tested, and what it leaves out), the bound for the own checker (bound, bmc::Parameters::max_string_length), a reader of a String argument from the checker's witness (read: units, null, or an earlier argument's object), and encode and rebuild between the interpreter's JStr and a witness's units. A String outside the domain (too long, null where not nullable, not code units) is refused by each, never cut. Verified by four unit tests and by lib/tests/values.rs, whose refutations now read their witnesses through read and rebuild every String in the interpreter's replay through rebuild, checked to encode back; the whole lib suite passes, the integration contract included (one untouched timing test of bmc::bits failed once under load and passed alone and on the rerun).

values::adapter still refuses a String, now saying the adapter is built and what a check lacks: the wiring that would let a regression or property check take a String parameter (the harness declaring it, the bound passed to the checker, jbmc::JbmcResult::arguments and the replay rebuilding it) is in the objects stream's files, and is recorded under Progress as an interface request. The briefs disagree here: the integration contract's V1 row (v1_a_symbolic_string_crosses_the_proof_boundary) accepts only the values stream's refusal, and the values brief makes V1's crossing of the proof boundary this stream's row, while the main brief's ownership gives harness/, equivalence.rs and property.rs to objects. Registering the adapter before that wiring would fail the contract's V1 row on another stream's files, so it waits for it.

### application-core values V2 step 1: the own checker runs the immutable-list models, keeping order, duplicates and aliases (verification pending)

change `qmtpnxsuzpsp` · [log `1f1361f8a1d2`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/1f1361f8a1d23edd39733d20208c0700d941530f2b677947e506bd2306ad4548.jsonl.gz)

V2's audit, then its first step. The models in lib/models/java/util (List.of, List.copyOf, ImmutableCollections' List12, ListN, ListItr) are the JDK's lists step for step with no JDK call, but were marked JBMC only, so the tool's own checker met List.of as the gap jdk-static-method and no check reached a list. models::CHECKER_RUNS now lists them. The checker calls their static methods as application methods, runs ImmutableCollections' initializer and holds its statics (ClassPath::checker_class, the one empty list and a list of one's sentinel), and treats AbstractCollection()'s empty constructor as exact. The gap scan walks the same methods and counts an interface call on a list or its iterator as no gap where the models implement it (gaps::dispatched_to_models). Any other java.util collection the checker could hold is made by a JDK call that is a gap where it's made, so copyOf of an ArrayList is still refused by name.

Reproducer: lib/tests/values.rs runs the checker on harness-shaped methods (tests/fixtures/values/values/Lists.java) that make lists the way a harness would: List.of over 0 to 3 constructor-made lines, any two of which may be one object. Before this change all of them met the jdk-static-method gap. Now the basket fixture's three rewrites are proved. Its four defects are refuted: a duplicate skipped, the last line for the first, a copy for the element, and an alias between elements. So is a wrong claim that two elements are two lines. size, isEmpty and the iterator behave as the JDK's; get out of range throws the JDK's class (List12 IndexOutOfBounds, ListN ArrayIndexOutOfBounds); null elements and changes are refused; copyOf of such a list is the list itself. Every refutation is replayed on a JVM and in the interpreter. Evidence level: tested.

The conformance corpus changed. 12 of its list claims that had no own-checker verdict are now decided, each as the JVM decides it. Their records are updated and lib/benchmark/conformance.json is re-blessed. One assertion of tests/conformance.rs is narrowed: it read any claim that strict decides while advised stops on a gap as a scan seeing an unreachable gap. listCopyMutable's refutation is a violation on a path with no gap, which strict's documented rule lets stand, so the assertion now fails only on a strict proof that advised stops on. The corpus also found an interpreter bug: an immutable collection's iterator refused remove instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so one witness didn't replay. That is fixed (Native::Iterator records whether its collection is immutable). Found but not fixed, under Progress: the interpreter names every immutable list ListN, so getClass of a List12 differs from the JVM's. The whole lib suite passes. Job 20261108-070211-application-core-values-v2-step-1-the-co runs the corpus's two JBMC tests (engine jbmc and auto, and auto --confirm, which now confirms the checker's list proofs). Expected to pass.

### application-core values V2 step 2: the list value adapter, its domain and model digest, the harness's Java, witness reader, encoding and rebuilding

change `qxpvnsmlnxpo` · [log `367614d26edf`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/367614d26edfe8c8d2e7915909a5ffe5bef6e4af67ad23f8fe113f27cf180cff.jsonl.gz)

values::ListAdapter is the value adapter for one bounded immutable-list family: lists List.of makes over at most max_length (up to 10) objects of one application class, null among them where the domain says so. Its domain is the shared ValueDomain of kind list, with the model's evidence (values::list_model: the list models with the SHA-256 of their bytecode, values::list_model_digest, so that a change in a model changes the evidence's identity; level tested on JDK 25.0.5; what it leaves out). Since the own checker runs the list models (V2 step 1), a list needs no symbolic form: a harness makes one as an application would, by List.of over max_length objects it made by the construction plan, from int choices the checker is free in (ListAdapter::choices, admitted, java): null, the length, and for each element after the first which made object it is, so that every pattern of duplicates and aliases is a choice. ListAdapter::read gives the witness's list as the plan's nodes in order; encode and rebuild go between it and the interpreter's list through values::Nodes (ValueAdapter's methods now take the run's plan objects; a String ignores them), rebuilding by the interpreter's own List.of. A list outside the family, longer than the bound, holding an object the plan didn't make, or a list of Strings, is refused by name, never cut or copied in.

Verified by five unit tests in values.rs and a new end-to-end test in lib/tests/values.rs, which generates a harness-shaped class from the adapter's own Java over the basket's kernels, runs the own checker on it (merging from the start and never), proves total, first (identity), clearAll and a nullable total, and refutes a skipped duplicate, a reordering, a copy for the element, an alias between mutable elements and a nullable domain's null. Each witness is read through the adapter and replayed on the JVM and, through the adapter's rebuilt lists, in the interpreter, which must observe the difference; each rebuilt list encodes back as its witness. Sabotaging the adapter's picks makes the test fail. The whole lib suite passes. Evidence level tested; no job.

values::adapter still refuses a list parameter by name: making it in a harness and rebuilding it in the replay is the objects stream's wiring, recorded under the brief's Progress as an interface request, with two points for the merge (a bound for String elements in the shared ElementKind, and the frozen basket claims' model evidence, level modelled, differing from the adapter's).

### application-core values V3 step 1: an evidence record per modelled String and list operation, checked against boundary cases on the JVM, the interpreter and the own checker

change `soumrxslppon` · [log `6a3c9bc013b3`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/6a3c9bc013b339f246b4ed7a0529e3546b851612c35dd22c95773ce48fcaaf37.jsonl.gz)

values::OPERATIONS holds one record (values::OperationEvidence) for each of the 14 operations the values models implement: for Strings the literal, the compiler's concatenation, length, isEmpty, charAt, equals and startsWith; for lists List.of's fixed forms, copyOf, size, isEmpty, get, the iterator's path, and the changes the lists refuse. Each record has its model family, what implements it in the own checker, the interpreter and for JBMC, the JDK it was sampled on (25.0.5), the inputs it admits, the exceptions it was seen to throw, what it leaves out, and its level, which is tested and never proved.

The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/values/values/Operations.java has 86 boundary cases. lib/tests/values.rs runs each one on the JVM, in the interpreter, and in the own checker through a generated method that asserts the JVM's outcome: a String by its code units, an exception by its exact class. The test fails unless all three agree, unless the exceptions each record's cases throw are exactly the ones it lists, and unless every String method the checker models on content has a record. All three engines agreed on every case. Three sabotages each fail the test: a missing exception in a record, 42 wrong expected values, and the wrong exception class for a List12's get. The whole lib suite passes. Strict gap detection and the bound sweep are next.

**Reply:**

The interpreter now holds Strings as UTF-16 code units, the same way the JVM does. That's the first step of V1, committed as `lkvnqurn` on this stream's branch.

**What was wrong.** The interpreter, which replays every witness, stored a String as Rust UTF-8 text. Every isolated surrogate silently became U+FFFD:
- `"\uD800".equals("\uFFFD")` and `"\uD800".equals("\uDC00")` both returned true.
- `charAt` returned 65533 instead of the surrogate.
- `substring` turned the halves of a split surrogate pair into two U+FFFD.

**The fix.** A new type, `interp::JStr`, holds the code units of every String and `StringBuilder`, and every modelled operation works on code units as the JDK does. It also fixes several smaller wrong answers:
- `reverse` broke surrogate pairs.
- `setLength(-1)` clamped to 0 instead of throwing.
- `append(CharSequence, int, int)` appended the whole sequence.
- `strip` and `isBlank` used Rust's idea of whitespace, not Java's.
- `new String(char[])` was refused; it's modelled now.

Operations that depend on Unicode's tables (case conversion, `equalsIgnoreCase`, `Integer.parseInt` on non-ASCII text) are now refused by name rather than answered for the wrong text.

**What the adapter does** (`values::StringAdapter`):

- **Out-of-domain values:** a String that is too long, a null where the domain doesn't allow one, or a malformed code unit is refused by each function, never shortened.
- **Tests:** four new unit tests. `lib/tests/values.rs` now reads every counterexample's Strings through `read`, rebuilds them through `rebuild` to replay them in the interpreter, and checks that they encode back to the same units.

I committed V2 step 2 as `qxpvnsml`: `values::ListAdapter`, the value adapter for lists that `List.of` makes over objects of one application class.

**What it does:**
- **Domain:** a list of up to 10 elements (`List.of`'s fixed forms), with the element class, whether the list may be null, and the model's evidence. The evidence includes a SHA-256 of the list models' bytecode, so a change to a model changes its identity. Its level is `tested`, never `proved`.
- **Making the list:** a harness makes the list the way an application would. The own checker picks the length and, for each element after the first, which already-made object it is. That covers every pattern of duplicates and aliases.
- **Witnesses and replay:** `read` turns a witness into the list's elements in order. `encode` and `rebuild` move a list between the interpreter and the witness.
- **Refusals:** a list from outside the family (an `ArrayList`), one past the bound, one holding an object the plan didn't make, and a list of Strings are each refused by name, never cut.

**Verification:**
- Five unit tests cover the adapter on its own.
- A new end-to-end test in `lib/tests/values.rs` builds a harness-shaped class from the adapter's own Java over the basket's kernels and runs the own checker on it. The correct rewrites prove (`total`, `first` by identity, `clearAll`, and a nullable `total`).
